ai_summary: Xtelify Limited experienced a 503 error spike during a live event, captured in ticket ERE-3110. The core problem was a brief but significant downstream impact, lasting under 40 seconds, in which 5xx errors were served downstream due to negative caching. This was caused by an overload of a Cloud Interconnect region stemming from an attack on TikTok, which triggered self-suspension of multiple machines in the region, compounded by the lack of a failover path at GCI. Because current RA feedback cycle times prevent traffic from being shifted sooner via mapper, the issue was mitigated by relying on product and configuration workarounds to use an alternate path. The planned long-term mitigation is config optimizations to work around issues at the CI tier.

JIOSTAR INDIA PRIVATE LIMITED (ticket ERE-3143) experienced performance degradation during the Jio WPL match on January 10, 2026, when flit overload occurred on two machines in r40697. The core problem stemmed from unexpected high-bandwidth segment traffic hitting the pristine live streaming workflow, where only child manifest calls were expected. The root cause was a client-side bug in the customer's MediaTailor/AWS setup that incorrectly routed ad segments and video segments into the pristine workflow. LinkedIn Corporation's account experienced a problem where the modify Access-Control-Allow-Origin (ACAO) rule stopped working after XML Optimization was enabled. The root cause was an incorrect configuration that modified the ACAO response header at the client-request metadata stage, where response headers are not available; this had previously appeared to work due to legacy template behavior, but XML Optimization enforced stricter stage execution and exposed the misconfiguration. The issue was resolved in v178 by removing the match:metadata-stage = client-request condition, allowing the header modification to occur at the correct stage and restoring the expected ACAO header behavior. The fix was validated and confirmed post-deployment, and the correct usage of metadata stages was communicated to prevent similar misconfigurations. As a long-term mitigation, the team plans to introduce validation checks, warnings, or improved documentation in Property Manager to prevent configuring response header modifications at unsupported metadata stages.

CBS Interactive Inc. (ticket ERE-3150) experienced an issue where fail-action requests were latching to an initial negatively cached response rather than executing as expected, because the fail-action metadata included a no-store directive. The root cause was that when negative cache already exists for a URL, fail-action requests get latched to the original negatively cached object, preventing the fail-action from running—since for fail-action to work, the edge must be allowed to forward the request and process or store the response. The issue was mitigated by adjusting the fail-action metadata to remove or relax the no-store directive, allowing the edge to forward requests and properly execute failover instead of latching to negative cache. Reviewing the negative cache settings was also recommended to ensure the fail-action logic is not bypassed. As a long-term mitigation, the configuration will be refined to align fail-action and negative caching behavior, ensuring failover logic isn't bypassed due to cached error responses.

CBS Interactive Inc. (ticket ERE-3154) removed Akamai from their CDN rotation during NFL playoff coverage on Saturday 1/17/26 after a moderate spike in edge 504 errors. The root cause was that fail-action requests were latched to the original negatively cached object because the fail-action metadata included no-store, preventing the edge from forwarding and processing the request as expected. As a mitigation, the configuration was fixed by removing the invalid metadata-stage constraint and ensuring response headers are modified only in supported stages. The planned long-term mitigation is to introduce validation, warnings, and improved documentation in Property Manager/Optimize XML to prevent unsupported configurations and enforce correct stage usage.

Schneider Electric Industries SAS reported an issue (ERE-3156) where failover metadata tags behave incorrectly when multiple failover behaviors match and last-match-win is expected. The core problem is that Property Manager does not generate a path tag when "Modify Incoming Path" is set to No, nor a preserve-query-string tag when "Include Query String" is set to No, so a tag applied by an earlier behavior with the option set to Yes remains active even when a later matching behavior sets the same option to No. The root cause is that setting "Include Query String" to Yes generates `<preserve-query-string>on</preserve-query-string>`, while setting it to No generates no tag at all, leaving no way to override the earlier value further down in the configuration. It was tested separately that the `<preserve-query-string>off</preserve-query-string>` tag works, and ticket DPEXREQ-1128 was raised to determine whether this behavior is intentional by design or requires changes. Both the short-term and long-term mitigation plans are to follow up on DPEXREQ-1128.

Luxottica Group s.p.a. reported that an MP4 video failed to play on Safari while working correctly on Chrome and Firefox. Testing with a separate property (cache ON, POC OFF) on an object cached for 7 days confirmed that range requests were not honored, which was determined to be expected behavior. No mitigation was applied because the Content-Length is correctly ignored when Transfer-Encoding is also present, and no long-term mitigation was planned.

Charles Schwab reported slow DNS resolution over Cloud Interconnect (ticket ERE-3176, F-CS-10785532). The core problem was elevated DNS times, which were traced to the LL map entry for the region/serial not being present in the ghost cache on initial or infrequently repeated requests; because each ghost's LL map cache has a defined limit, older entries are evicted when the cache fills, so entries made with delayed frequency fail to persist and report higher DNS times. The issue was mitigated by making regular, frequent requests to keep the LL map entry available in cache and thereby eliminate the elevated DNS times. As a long-term mitigation, the SRMM team increased the cache limit from 200 to 1000 to work around these issues. Given the growing customer base, an even higher cache limit is anticipated as a future requirement.

The home24 SE account (ticket ERE-3371) experienced ERR_CHUNK_INCOMPLETE errors when H2G2O was enabled and the origin replied with an empty body. The root cause is a protocol translation bug in the Akamai Ghost H2G2O layer, which misinterprets an empty DATA frame carrying the END_STREAM flag as a 1-byte object size, throwing a ChunkedEofBeforeFirstHexDigitException, emitting a faulty Content-Length: 1 header, and prematurely dropping the client connection. As an immediate mitigation, the customer temporarily disabled H2G2O in their property configuration (or reverted Staging to version 279), forcing Ghost to fall back to an HTTP/1.1 forwarding path that correctly processes the origin's empty chunked responses. A permanent software fix is being engineered by the Ghost Core HTTP/2 team under tracking tickets GREL-5726 and GHOST-7972, refactoring the proxy engine to compute an empty DATA frame with END_STREAM as 0 bytes and translate it to a Content-Length: 0 header, with global production rollout expected by early July 2026. Long term, the team will monitor the GREL-5726 deployment, coordinate with the customer to safely re-enable H2G2O with regression testing against the /healthcheck endpoint, and integrate this HTTP/2 framing edge case into Ghost's automated test suites to prevent future regressions.
